pr_title: Allow PcapWriteHandler to output PCAP files larger than 2GB
pr_body:
Motivation:

PcapWriteHandler should be able to support large files but is currently limited to 2GB due to the usage of int without wrapping.

Modifications:

segmentNumber and ackNumber are now long values to support uint32 values. segmentNumber and ackNumber wrap around when the uint32 max is reached. Ported unit test from https://github.com/apple/swift-nio-extras/pull/85

Result:

Fixes #11543

issue_context.title: Make `PcapWriteHandler` support files bigger than 2 GB
issue_context.body:
### Expected behavior
`PcapWriteHandler` should support large files, say 10 GB or 1 TB.

### Actual behavior
Currently, `PcapWriteHandler` can only support files up to 2 GB because it uses 32-bit Integer.

### Steps to reproduce
N/A

### Minimal yet complete reproducer code (or URL to code)
Just capture data big enough to exceed 2 GB.

### Netty version
4.1.66.Final

### JVM version (e.g. `java -version`)
openjdk version "1.8.0_302"
OpenJDK Runtime Environment Corretto-8.302.08.1 (build 1.8.0_302-b08)
OpenJDK 64-Bit Server VM Corretto-8.302.08.1 (build 25.302-b08, mixed mode)

### OS version (e.g. `uname -a`)
Windows 10 Pro x64

@hyperxpro are the fields in question `sendSegmentNumber` and `receiveSegmentNumber`[1]? 

I see that we do not guard against integer overflow while accumulating bytes in these fields[2], perhaps we can do that before supporting larger payloads?

[1] https://github.com/netty/netty/blob/4.1/handler/src/main/java/io/netty/handler/pcap/PcapWriteHandler.java#L97-L103
[2] https://github.com/netty/netty/blob/4.1/handler/src/main/java/io/netty/handler/pcap/PcapWriteHandler.java#L284
Yes, we need to guard them against overflow. Norman did share swift-nio pcap where they fixed larger payloads and overflow. Lemme try to find it.

review_comments: We should produce a 5G file and try to read it using Wireshark just to be double-sure.
@normanmaurer I'll have time today to look into this and address any issues I find.

Found 2 issues directly related to this PR while using Wireshark to look at the generated 5GB pcap. Those will be addressed.

Noticed two other issues present in 4.1.

1. If the payload is larger than 65495 for TCP, the length field in the IP packet is incorrect due to the length being a ushort. UDP will have a similar problem.
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/155cec08-767f-4efc-a2c5-c9c04718bd75)
2. When the PcapWriteHandler is attached to a TCP server, the FIN messages have incorrect segment and ack numbers. 
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/236c3109-558d-4fa2-8cce-5fa05503ebc0)


I will try to find the time to address these here with unit tests

For TCP, the payload can just be split into multiple PCAP entries. 
For UDP, I imagine it could just log that it received too large of a payload.
Alright, all of the above have been handled. Tested large PCAP files and those show correctly in Wireshark now.
